questions.question_text: Two numbers have a sum of $50$ and a difference of $12$. What are the two numbers?

options.why: Split the sum equally, ignoring that the numbers must differ by $12$.
Used $12$ as one number and $50-12=38$ as the other instead of solving the pair.
Found the larger number correctly but wrote the difference $12$ as the second number.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the larger and $y$ the smaller number.
$x+y=50 \quad (1)$
$x-y=12 \quad (2)$
$(1)+(2):\ 2x=62$
$x=31$
$31+y=50$
$y=19$
The two numbers are $31$ and $19$.

questions.question_text: Two pens and one notebook cost \$8. One pen and one notebook cost \$5. Find the cost of a pen and the cost of a notebook.

options.why: Swapped the two prices, assigning each cost to the wrong item.
Halved the \$8 for one pen, ignoring the notebook in that purchase.
Read the \$5 total as the notebook price instead of solving for it.

questions.solution_text:
Let $p$ be the cost of a pen and $n$ the cost of a notebook, in dollars.
$2p+n=8 \quad (1)$
$p+n=5 \quad (2)$
$(1)-(2):\ p=3$
$3+n=5$
$n=2$
A pen costs \$3 and a notebook costs \$2.

questions.question_text: A muffin costs \$1 more than a cookie. Three muffins and two cookies cost \$13. Find the cost of a cookie and the cost of a muffin.

options.why: Swapped the two prices, making the muffin cheaper than the cookie.
Used the \$1 difference as the cookie price without forming the total equation.
Solved $5c=10$ as $c=5$ by dividing by $2$ instead of $5$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $c$ be the cost of a cookie and $m$ the cost of a muffin, in dollars.
$m=c+1 \quad (1)$
$3m+2c=13 \quad (2)$
$3(c+1)+2c=13$
$3c+3+2c=13$
$5c=10$
$c=2$
$m=2+1$
$=3$
A cookie costs \$2 and a muffin costs \$3.

questions.question_text: Maria is $4$ times as old as her son. The difference in their ages is $27$ years. How old is each person?

options.why: Swapped the ages, making the son older than his mother.
Took $27$ as Maria's age instead of the difference between the ages.
Read $27$ as the son's age, then multiplied by $4$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $m$ be Maria's age and $s$ her son's age.
$m=4s \quad (1)$
$m-s=27 \quad (2)$
$4s-s=27$
$3s=27$
$s=9$
$m=4(9)$
$=36$
Maria is $36$ years old and her son is $9$ years old.

questions.question_text: A jar holds \$5 made up of $20$-cent and $50$-cent coins, with $16$ coins in all. How many of each coin are there?

options.why: Swapped the two coin counts.
Split the $16$ coins equally, ignoring the \$5 total value.
Assumed every coin was a $20$-cent coin.

questions.solution_text:
Let $t$ be the number of $20$-cent coins and $f$ the number of $50$-cent coins.
$t+f=16 \quad (1)$
$0.20t+0.50f=5 \quad (2)$
$(2)\times 10:\ 2t+5f=50 \quad (3)$
$(1)\times 2:\ 2t+2f=32 \quad (4)$
$(3)-(4):\ 3f=18$
$f=6$
$t+6=16$
$t=10$
There are ten $20$-cent coins and six $50$-cent coins.

questions.question_text: A rectangle has a perimeter of $40$ cm, and its length is $4$ cm more than its width. Find the width and length.

options.why: Swapped length and width, making the length shorter than the width.
Used $l+w=40$ instead of halving the perimeter to get $l+w=20$.
Split $20$ equally, ignoring the $4$ cm difference in the sides.

questions.solution_text:
Let $l$ be the length and $w$ the width, in centimetres.
$2l+2w=40 \quad (1)$
$l=w+4 \quad (2)$
$l+w=20$
$(w+4)+w=20$
$2w+4=20$
$2w=16$
$w=8$
$l=8+4$
$=12$
The width is $8$ cm and the length is $12$ cm.

questions.question_text: Two adult and three child tickets cost \$74. Three adult and two child tickets cost \$76. Find the cost of an adult ticket and a child ticket.

options.why: Swapped the adult and child prices.
Forgot the $3(14)$ child term when back-substituting, using $2a=74$.
Solved $5c=70$ as $c=10$ by dividing by $7$ instead of $5$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $a$ be the cost of an adult ticket and $c$ the cost of a child ticket, in dollars.
$2a+3c=74 \quad (1)$
$3a+2c=76 \quad (2)$
$(1)\times 3:\ 6a+9c=222 \quad (3)$
$(2)\times 2:\ 6a+4c=152 \quad (4)$
$(3)-(4):\ 5c=70$
$c=14$
$2a+3(14)=74$
$2a=32$
$a=16$
An adult ticket costs \$16 and a child ticket costs \$14.

questions.question_text: A shop blends \$8 per kg coffee with \$12 per kg coffee to make $10$ kg worth \$9 per kg. How much of each type is used?

options.text: $7.5$ kg of the \$8 coffee and $2.5$ kg of the \$12 coffee
$2.5$ kg of the \$8 coffee and $7.5$ kg of the \$12 coffee
options.why: Swapped the amounts, using more of the dearer coffee even though \$9 is nearer \$8.
Split the $10$ kg equally, ignoring that \$9 is not halfway between \$8 and \$12.

options.text: $6$ kg of the \$8 coffee and $4$ kg of the \$12 coffee
options.why: Estimated from the price gap instead of forming and solving the value equation.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the kg of \$8 coffee and $y$ the kg of \$12 coffee.
$x+y=10 \quad (1)$
$8x+12y=9(10) \quad (2)$
$8x+12y=90$
$y=10-x$
$8x+12(10-x)=90$
$8x+120-12x=90$
$-4x=-30$
$x=7.5$
$y=10-7.5$
$=2.5$
The shop uses $7.5$ kg of the \$8 coffee and $2.5$ kg of the \$12 coffee.
